                                Statement by

          H.E. Mr. Saleumxay Kommasith, Minister of Foreign Affairs

     of the Lao People’s Democratic Republic at the 72" Session of the United
                           Nations General Assembly

                        23 September 2017, New York

Mr. President,

     At  the  outset, on  behalf of the  delegation  of the Lao  People’s
Democratic Republic,  I would like to extend my congratulations to Your
Excellency Miroslav Lajéak on your election as the President of this 7284
Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).  I am confident
that with your extensive diplomatic experience, you will guide this Session
of the General Assembly with a great success. We stand ready to extend
our full support and cooperation to you in the discharge of your noble duty.
Likewise, may I also extend my profound congratulations to His Excellency
Peter Thomson for the successful completion of his tenure as the President
of the 71" Session of the UNGA.

     Once   again,  may   I  take   this  opportunity   to  extend  my
congratulations to His Excellency Antonio Guterres on his appointment as
the Secretary-General of the United Nations and for his initiative on the
management reform of the United Nations so that this organization can
respond effectively to the current global challenges. I hope that such efforts
will contribute to the attainment of the aims and objectives of the Charter

of the United Nations.

    MayI  join other delegates in extending our deep sympathy to the
countries in Latin America and the Caribbean which have been severely

affected by recent natural disasters.




Mr. President,

     Today the current global geopolitical landscape  is fraught with a
myriad of challenges which pose a major threat to peace and security and
adversely hamper development of countries and  regions  in the world.
Therefore, it calls for our concerted efforts to overcome those obstacles and
challenges so that people in different countries and various regions of the
world can live their lives in a durable peace and prosperity. That is why,
the choice of the theme: “focusing on people: striving for peace and a decent
life for  all on a sustainable planet”  for the  72"" UNGA  is apt  as  the
international community  is focusing on the implementation of the 2030

                                                      1

agenda for sustainable development that has promised  to leave no one

behind.

        It  is my firm  belief that peace and security remain the common
aspiration of the international community. As such, in order to maintain
and promote peace and development,  it is incumbent upon us to enhance
collaboration so that peace and sustainable development can prevail in our
world.  The United Nations,  the only universal organization with the
mandates   to  maintain  and  promote  peace  and  cooperation   for
development, has to be in the forefront.  To realize these objectives, the
United Nations needs to be reformed  in a manner  it can respond to the

current needs and pressing challenges today.

     The Lao PDR earnestly hopes to see the world without nuclear and
other weapons of mass destruction. In this context, we welcome the recent
adoption of the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons which, we
also signed two days ago. But we are well aware that we still have an uphill
task ahead of us for this Treaty  to enter into force and be effectively
implemented. Therefore, the international community has to redouble  its
efforts in this respect.




Mr. President,

     Throughout the past decades, we have witnessed that many countries
in the world have experienced a sustained economic growth and rapid
development, which have  lifted hundreds of millions  of people out of
poverty. Thanks to peace and security which have been prerequisites and
essential for social and economic advancement of nations. At the same time,

improvement of people’s well-being will have positive impact on political
stability and  social order and helps to reduce conflicts. Past experience
shows that settling disputes by peaceful means and through diplomatic
solutions is the best way as it is more durable and causes no loss of lives and
properties of the people. As such,  it  is important for the international
community to further build mutual trust, flexibility and jointly address the
root cause of the problem. In this spirit, the Lao PDR calls on all parties
involved  in the disputes or conflicts  in various regions of the world  to
exercise the utmost restraint and resolve such conflicts through diplomatic

                                                     2

and peaceful means so as to deescalate the tensions as we firmly believe
that  only  peaceful  environment  can form  a  fundamental ground  for
advancing national social and economic development.

     The Lao PDR welcomes  the  re-establishment  of the  diplomatic
relations between the United States of America and the Republic of Cuba
and earnestly hopes that such relations will be enhanced, leading to the
lifting of the embargo in the near future, thereby, bringing about the real
benefits to the peoples of the two countries as well as to the region and the
world at large. Likewise, the Lao PDR also hopes that the Palestinian issue
which has been lasted for many decades will be solved by peaceful means
with a view to creating two independent states of Palestine and Israel living
side by  side  in  peace,  security and  within  internationally  recognized
borders  as  stipulated  in  the  relevant  Resolutions  of the UN  Security

Council.




Mr. President,

      This year ASEAN turns 50, over the past 5 decades, ASEAN has gone
through a number of challenges and has adjusted  itself to the changing
regional and  international  environment, while  taking  into account  its
diversity and  particularities  in  the  region, and  has achieved  progress
gradually,  which  led  to  the  establishment  of the ASEAN  Economic
Community at the end of 2015.


     The most remarkable achievement of ASEAN is the maintenance of

peace,  security and  stability  in  the  region,  thus  serving  as  favorable
condition for ASEAN Member States in pursuit of their respective socio-
economic developments as well as regional economic integration.  At the
same time, ASEAN has strengthened  its relations with external  parties,
especially   its  Dialogue  Partners  in  a  substantive  and  comprehensive
manner based on mutual benefit, and importantly, ASEAN centrality has
been  recognized  by   all  external  partners  under  ASEAN-initiated
mechanisms.   Countries  in  the  region and beyond  are keen  to  forge
cooperation with ASEAN as  it provides a venue for them to participate in
the discussions on many important regional and international  issues of
common interest and concern, thus promoting mutual understanding and

                                                     3

trust among  participants  as  well  as  promoting  peace,  stability  and
development in the region and the world at large.



     The ASEAN’s achievements have been possible thanks to the ASEAN
Way,  which    is  an  important   factor,   especially  the  principles  of
“consultation and consensus” and “moving at a pace comfortable to all”.
ASEAN Way signifies ASEAN centrality and unity. ASEAN Way, in deed,
remains relevant and ASEAN will continue to uphold this principle in the

years to come.




Mr. President,

     The Lao PDR attaches great importance to the implementation of the
2030 agenda for sustainable development. Since their adoption, SDGs have
been streamlined into our current National Socio-Economic Development
Plan  for  (for 2016-2020) and  a National  Steering Committee  for  the
Implementation of the SDGs chaired by H.E. Prime Minister Thongloun
Sisoulith has been formally established. At the High-Level Political Forum
on Sustainable Development held in July, the Lao PDR has registered to
submit and present our Voluntary National Review in 2018, all of which
has demonstrated our Government’s firm  political will and unwavering
commitment to implement and achieve the SDGs as well as build a strong
foundation  to support our country’s aspirations  to graduate from  least
developing country status by 2020. In pursuance of fostering an enabling
environment conducive  for achieving sustainable development, the Lao
Government has taken an important initiative by adopting our national
SDGI18 entitled “Lives Safe from UXO” which was officially launched by
Prime Minister of the Lao PDR and former UN Secretary General Ban Ki-
moon in September 2016 at the sideline of the 8" ASEAN-UN Summit in
Vientiane. The SDG18 aims  to address specific development challenges
caused by unexploded ordnances to mitigate their impacts on the lives of
our people which will pave the way for improving the livelihood and well-
being of the rural population and enabling them  to contribute  to the
implementation of sustainable development agenda.





                                             4

Mr. President,

      Being  both  least developed and  land-locked,  the Lao PDR  has
continued to encounter various challenges that hinder our socio-economic
development and achievement of the agreed global development  goals.
Against this backdrop, the Lao PDR has pursued its development through
the  implementation  of  the  8"  Five-Year  National  Socio-Economic
Development Plan 2016-2020, the Strategy 2025 and the Vision 2030 aimed
at graduating from the LDC status and becoming a high-middle income
country by 2030. Towards this end, the Lao PDR_  pursues a policy of
transforming  from  a  land-locked  country  into  a  land-linked  hub,
facilitating  direct  connectivity  between  the  immediate  neighbouring
countries:  Viet Nam, Thailand and China and  the wider  region and
constituting   part  of  the  production  and  supply  chains  through
implementation of infrastructure  projects, improvement of logistics and
transport networks, for instance, the construction of a high speed railway
from  Vientiane  to Kunming,  improvement  of North-South  Economic
Corridor and East-West Economic Corridor, among others. These national
strategies are being implemented  as part of international and  regional
initiatives being undertaken such  as ASEAN Vision  2025, the ASEAN
Master Plan 2025 and China’s Belt and Road Initiative, in which, the Lao

PDR is a partner.




Mr. President,

        I am of the view that political will constitutes a fundamental principle
for attaining all agreed global development goals. Without firm political
commitment, we will not be able to turn sustainable development agenda
into  concrete  actions and  outcomes.  Therefore, my  delegation  firmly
believes that development remains an integral part and a top priority for
ensuring international peace, security and human rights, all of which are
closely  linked.  Against  this  backdrop, we  call  on  the  international
community to increase concerted efforts to ensure that development brings
equal benefits for all countries. The Lao Government once again, reaffirms
its strong determination  to work more  closely  with  the  international
community to realize the Agenda 2030 for Sustainable Development as well



                                                 5

as to achieve our national development objectives of eradicating poverty,
laying a solid foundation for LDC graduation, turning the country into an
industrialized and modern nation and moving towards the direction of
green and sustainable development that benefits for all the people, thereby,
ensuring that no one in the country is left behind.





                       Thank You.
